title: Quota-sensitive dynamic routing with ephemeral burst buckets and eviction safeguards
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Free, paid, and enterprise customers share serving capacity across regions. Under bursty demand (e.g., PLG spikes or enterprise batch jobs), we need a routing policy that: 1) respects plan quotas, 2) allows short-lived bursts for latency-sensitive paid calls, 3) gracefully demotes traffic when quotas are exhausted, and 4) avoids cascading failures from eviction or regional spillovers. Current tier routing is static and often either blocks or sends disproportionate traffic to fallback variants, causing tail latency spikes and unexpected quota exhaustion.
acceptance_criteria: Tiered routes honor per-tenant token quotas and ephemeral burst buckets in steady and burst traffic tests
Paid tier requests get bounded short-lived priority (burst token allowance) without starving free tier beyond configured thresholds
Fallback to cheaper model variants occurs with soft-degradation (probabilistic sampling + rate-limited demotion) rather than wholesale eviction
No cross-region hotspots after simulated regional outage and graceful spillback applied
SLOs: 99th latency for paid tier remains within 1.25x baseline during 30s burst tests; platform error rate increase <= 2%
Comprehensive unit / integration tests and a canary rollout with automatic rollback on SLA regressions
design_decisions: Ephemeral burst buckets: allocate a small, time-windowed token pool per tenant+tier (configurable, default 500 tokens per 60s) to cover short spikes without touching long-term quota
Admission controller: implement a quota-aware admission filter at the router layer that checks (burst_bucket, plan_quota, steady_rate) and produces one of {Accept, Soft-Demote, Hard-Deny}
Soft-Demote policy: probabilistic downgrade to fallback model variant with an adjustable sampling weight and a rate limiter to avoid sudden throughput shifts
Regional affinity: prefer same-region capacity while allowing controlled spillback to adjacent regions using spill_tokens to avoid oscillation
Hierarchical decision order: 1) fast path for enterprise plans with reserved share, 2) burst bucket check for paid, 3) plan quota check, 4) soft-demote sampling, 5) hard deny
Observability: emit detailed reason tags (admission_result, quota_bucket, burst_remaining, routing_target, demote_prob) for every routed request
implementation_steps: Router: add burst_bucket state keyed by tenant_id+tier persisted in fast in-memory store (LRU backed). Implement atomic token burn for admission checks
Admission logic: new policy module in routing service that returns decision and metadata tags
Demotion engine: extend model catalog to register fallback variants with demotion weights and enforce demote rate limits per tenant
Regional spillback: add spill_tokens and backoff timers per region to prevent thrash during outage
API: expose per-tenant config knobs (burst_size, burst_window, demote_max_rps) in Console and Dedicated manifests
Tests: synthetic traffic runner for steady/burst/regional-failover scenarios; add regression suite to CI
Docs: update routing policy docs, Console UI tooltips, and runbook
Telemetry: add metrics and traces; integrate thresholds into rollout monitors and incident alerts
rollout_plan: Unit tests + integration tests in PR; bench tests in perf cluster
Stage rollout to internal orgs and 3 low-risk customers for 48h with heavy burst simulation
Canary at 5% traffic for 24h with rollback on metric regressions (latency P99, error rate, quota_violation rate)
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with monitoring windows
Post-rollout: 7-day watch and follow-up tuning for burst sizes and demote weights
qa_plan: Unit tests for token accounting (concurrent burns) and overflow conditions
Integration tests with model catalog demotion and fallback models
Load test scenarios: steady 100qps, burst 2k qps for 30s, multi-tenant mixed workloads
Chaos test: simulate region outage and validate spillback/backoff behavior
Security review for tenancy isolation and attacker-abuse cases (fake tenant token exhaustion)
ops_runbook: How to toggle 'quota_dynamic_routing' feature flag per org
Investigating elevated HardDeny rates: check tenant quota, burst bucket exhaustion, and downstream model availability
Emergency rollback: disable feature flag and flush ephemeral state; notify SRE and on-call owners
Alert thresholds: demote_rate > 5% sustained for 10m triggers paging; routing_latency_p99 > baseline*1.5 for 5m triggers investigation
Logging: sample traces with admission tags for high-latency requests (1 in 200)
